title: Design and ship open-source cmdrvl umbrella porcelain CLI for agent data workflows
description:
Moved from cmdrvl/.github bd-63g on 2026-11-24 (the .github repo no longer carries a bead tracker). Original dependency bd-yn3 is closed.

## Background & Rationale
The CMD+RVL spine ships 14 separate bare single-word binaries (`vacuum`, `hashbytes`, `fingerprint`, `profile`, `shape`, `rvl`, `canon`, `verify`, `assess`, `lock`, `pack`, `benchmark`, `veil`, `airlock`). While atomic Unix binaries are great for composable pipelines, this creates two real adoption bottlenecks for AI agents:

1. **Global PATH collision & discovery overhead:** Installing 14 generic single-word binaries risks OS/dev tool collisions (`hash` and `benchmark` already collided in Homebrew) and forces agents to inspect each binary individually.
2. **High multi-command ceremony:** Common end-to-end tasks require chaining 3-5 commands (`vacuum | hashbytes | fingerprint | lock`, `shape && rvl && pack seal`), which is why `cmdrvl/receipts` had to wrap them in bash scripts.

## Goal
Design and ship a thin, open-source `cmdrvl` umbrella porcelain CLI (following Pattern B from multi-tool family ergonomics: family-aware orchestrator binary) that dispatches to or embeds the atomic spine tools without replacing them.

## Core Surfaces
- `cmdrvl capabilities --json` — consolidated family catalog of installed spine versions, shared exit codes, envelope schema, and per-binary capabilities pointers.
- `cmdrvl doctor --json` / `cmdrvl --robot-triage` — single-call fleet health & version-drift check across all installed spine binaries.
- `cmdrvl inspect <file> [--sheet <name>] --json` — zero-retention single-file structural profiler (CSV/TSV/JSONL/Parquet/XLSX).
- `cmdrvl diff <old> <new> [--key K] --json` — runs `shape` gate then `rvl` explanation in one round-trip with structured stop handling.
- `cmdrvl receipt <old> <new> [--key K] --out <dir>` — native Rust equivalent of `receipts-csv` (`shape` -> `rvl` -> `pack seal` -> `pack verify`).
- `cmdrvl <subtool> ...` pass-through so teams can avoid polluting global PATH with 14 bare binaries if desired.

## Testing & Verification
- E2E tests covering `cmdrvl capabilities --json`, `cmdrvl doctor --json`, `cmdrvl diff`, `cmdrvl inspect`, and `cmdrvl receipt` against real fixtures.
- Determinism and non-TTY tests across all umbrella verbs.
acceptance_criteria: Architecture ADR and working open-source cmdrvl umbrella CLI shipping capabilities --json, doctor --json, inspect, diff, and receipt with E2E tests.

title: Audit and improve github.com/cmdrvl accessibility for agents and humans
description:
Moved from cmdrvl/.github bd-3m5 on 2026-11-24 (the .github repo no longer carries a bead tracker). NOTE: the findings below are from 2026-09-03 and PARTLY STALE: the broken profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md link and install guidance were fixed by .github bd-xk6/bd-yn3 (closed 2026-11-24); finding 5 (cmdrvl.com llms.txt / llms-full.txt) lives outside the repos in this swarm. Re-check each finding before acting on it.

Audit and improve how github.com/cmdrvl and its agent-facing surfaces communicate the spine tools (vacuum, hash, fingerprint, profile, shape, rvl, verify, benchmark, assess, canon, lock, pack, veil, airlock, twinning, regret) — especially the framing that these tools work as business-logic-as-information-artifacts primitives for agents (constraint sets, registries, schemas, fingerprints — not embedded code logic), which is the angle that resonated in a recent LinkedIn exchange (Vin's "AI needs business logic as information models, not code" post, 2026-09-03).

Findings from initial audit (2026-09-03):

1. Org profile README (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/README.md`, renders at github.com/cmdrvl) is actually already fairly strong — has concrete examples, a "Start Here" table, quick start, and a "For Agent Builders" section. Opportunity: sharpen the opening framing to lead with "these tools externalize business logic into declared, versioned artifacts (constraint sets, registries, schemas) instead of leaving it embedded in code or expecting an agent to infer it" — this is a stronger, more specific hook than the current "help agents answer hard data questions without hand-waving" opener.

2. **Broken link, confirmed bug**: the README's "For Agent Builders" section links to `./SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, but the actual file in the repo is named `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` (`cmdrvl/.github/profile/SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`) — a rename that never got the README link updated. Confirmed 404 via `gh api repos/cmdrvl/.github/contents/profile/SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`. `AGENT_PROMPT.md` (the other linked file) does exist and resolves fine.

3. The content of `SPINE_SYSTEM_PROMPT.md` itself is solid — compact (~38 lines), copy-paste-ready, covers the pipeline, report tools, refusal handling, self-discovery (`--describe`/`--schema`). Minor gap: it doesn't mention `veil` or `airlock` in the install line or tool list, even though the org README's Shipped Tools table does.

4. **cmdrvl.com already has a GitHub link** — present in the footer (`data-cmdrvl-footer-link="primary"` → `https://github.com/cmdrvl`) and in the homepage's schema.org `sameAs` JSON-LD. So "ensure github link on cmdrvl.com" is mostly done; worth a quick check on whether it should also be more prominent than footer-only (e.g., surfaced from a dedicated open-source/tools page or the main nav), given the open-source CLI layer is a distinct audience from the consulting/data-product visitors the rest of the site targets.

5. **Gap: cmdrvl.com's agent-facing surfaces (llms.txt, llms-full.txt) never mention the open-source spine tools at all.** Confirmed via `curl https://cmdrvl.com/llms.txt` and `/llms-full.txt` — both are entirely about the CMD+RVL consulting/data-product business (finance/procurement outcomes, evidence packs, MCP servers) with zero reference to github.com/cmdrvl, the spine tools, or a system-prompt link. An agent reading cmdrvl.com's own agent-facing index has no path to discover the open-source tools exist.

Scope for this epic: land the concrete fixes below, then re-review the whole surface end to end (org README opening framing, tool list completeness, cmdrvl.com llms.txt/llms-full.txt, and GitHub link prominence) against the accessibility bar Zac raised.

title: Add Homebrew formula for open-source cmdrvl umbrella CLI once published
description:
## Background
Once the open-source `cmdrvl` umbrella porcelain CLI (`cmdrvl capabilities --json`, `cmdrvl doctor`, `cmdrvl inspect`, `cmdrvl diff`, `cmdrvl receipt`) cuts its first release, users and agents should be able to install the whole workflow entry point with a single `brew install cmdrvl/tap/cmdrvl`.

## Deliverables
- Add `Formula/cmdrvl.rb` with macOS/Linux arm64/x86_64 bottles and SHA-256 verification.
- Document whether `cmdrvl` depends on individual spine formulae or bundles/manages them, with `test do` verifying `cmdrvl --version` and `cmdrvl capabilities --json`.
acceptance_criteria: brew install cmdrvl/tap/cmdrvl installs cleanly and passes brew test cmdrvl/tap/cmdrvl.

title: Add bin/spine-doctor shell script for pipeline health checks
description:
## Problem

There is no way to verify the spine pipeline is correctly installed and wired. After installing 7+ tools from the tap, a user (or agent) has to manually run each binary to check it exists, then mentally reconstruct the pipeline order from individual --describe outputs.

During the spring11 CRE extraction session, we discovered:
- \`profile --describe\` crashes (exit 2, "Failed to read operator.json")
- \`rvl\` is missing --describe, --schema, and --version entirely
- \`fingerprint --describe\` returns a different schema format than the rest
- The binary name (\`hashbytes\`) doesn't match the describe name (\`hash\`) or the formula name (\`cmdrvl-hash\`)

None of this was obvious until we tried each tool individually.

## Proposal

A shell script at \`bin/spine-doctor\` that:

1. Checks each known binary exists on PATH
2. Runs \`<tool> --version\` and reports version (or flags failure)
3. Runs \`<tool> --describe\` and flags failures or non-standard output
4. Assembles and prints the pipeline DAG from \`pipeline.upstream/downstream\`
5. Flags naming inconsistencies (binary vs describe name)
6. Reports an overall health status

Example output:
\`\`\`
spine-doctor

Tools:
  vacuum     0.1.0  ✓ describe ✓ schema
  hashbytes  0.2.0  ✓ describe ✓ schema  ⚠ name mismatch (describe: "hash")
  fingerprint 0.3.0 ⚠ describe (non-standard schema)  ✓ schema
  shape      0.2.0  ✓ describe  ✗ schema (not supported)
  profile    0.1.0  ✗ describe (exit 2)  ✓ schema
  rvl        ???    ✗ describe  ✗ schema  ✗ version
  lock       0.2.0  ✓ describe ✓ schema
  canon      (not installed)
  pack       (not installed)

Pipeline:
  vacuum → hashbytes → fingerprint → lock
                    ↘ shape → rvl
           profile ─────────→ (shape, rvl) [deferred in v0]

Health: 5/9 tools installed, 2 with --describe issues, 1 missing --version
\`\`\`

## Implementation notes

- Pure shell script, no dependencies beyond the tools themselves
- The tap already defines the canonical formula list — derive tool names from Formula/*.rb
- Could also check witness ledger health (\`~/.epistemic/witness.jsonl\` exists and is writable)
- Keep it simple: if it grows beyond ~100 lines, graduate to a real binary in its own repo
notes: Dependency note: spine-doctor will report issues that are being fixed in parallel (bd-25h rvl --describe, bd-1c4 profile --describe, bd-3mz fingerprint operator.v0, bd-1e0 hash naming). Implement after those fixes land for accurate baseline reporting. Consider P3 until prerequisites are done.
close_reason: Added bin/spine-doctor — checks all 9 tools for PATH presence, --version, --describe (operator.v0), --schema, name mismatches, and witness ledger health. 95 lines of pure bash, no external deps.

title: Resolve cmdrvl-hash / cmdrvl-benchmark formula naming friction and add tap README with verified install commands
description:
## Background & Evidence
Org docs (`cmdrvl/.github` README, `SYSTEM_PROMPT.md`, `AGENT_PROMPT.md`) tell users and agents to run `brew install cmdrvl/tap/hash` and `brew install cmdrvl/tap/benchmark` (and claim the latter installs `cmdrvl-benchmark`). In reality, `homebrew-tap` ships `Formula/cmdrvl-hash.rb` (installing `hashbytes`) and `Formula/cmdrvl-benchmark.rb` (installing `benchmark`). First-try installs fail immediately.

## Goal
Eliminate Homebrew installation friction and drift between formulae, installed binaries, and org documentation.

## Deliverables
- Add a clear `README.md` in `homebrew-tap` listing every formula, installed binary name, and verified copy-paste `brew install` commands (core set + full set).
- Decide and document Homebrew aliases or caveats for `cmdrvl-hash` (`hashbytes`) and `cmdrvl-benchmark` (`benchmark`), plus verify `vacuum.rb` documents its second installed binary `s3-to-vacuum`.
- Add a CI check verifying every formula passes `brew audit --strict` (or Ruby syntax + binary-name consistency check) and matches the tap README table.
acceptance_criteria: Tap README documents exact formula->binary mappings, caveats clarify hashbytes/benchmark/s3-to-vacuum, and CI validates formula table parity.
close_reason: Verified by independent verifier at eb18ee1 (git-archive extract): ruby -c on all Formula/*.rb, bin/check-tap, tests/check_tap_test.rb clean; ruby bin/check-tap = 16 formulae checked (syntax, binary mappings, 2 aliases, README install commands); ruby tests/check_tap_test.rb = 10 runs 0 failures; checker is local-only, no network/install. Formula->binary mapping cmdrvl-hash->hashbytes, cmdrvl-benchmark->benchmark, vacuum->vacuum+s3-to-vacuum agrees with README; caveats added to all 3 formulae; check-tap.yml runs both scripts. Scope: tap files only. Not verified: brew audit/install, alias resolution inside Homebrew (agent also disclosed).
